stage.name: Creational Patterns
stage.subtitle: Book chapter 9
stage.description: Factory, builder, prototype, and singleton patterns in PHP.

payload.markdown: This chapter covered some of the tricks that you can use to generate objects. I began by examining the Singleton pattern, which provides global access to a single instance. Next, I looked at the Factory Method pattern, which applies the principle of polymorphism to object generation. And I combined Factory Method with the Abstract Factory pattern to generate creator classes that instantiate sets of related objects. I also looked at the Prototype pattern and saw how object cloning can allow composition to be used in object generation. Finally, I examined two strategies for object creation: Service Locator and Dependency Injection.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Composition: Building classes from other objects instead of inheriting from them.
Dependency Injection: Receiving collaborators from outside instead of constructing them internally.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Polymorphism: Different classes responding to the same call each in their own way.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
